answer: Trust-graph capping: rewards flow along real payment edges, and a cluster of accounts can earn at most what its links to outside agents justify. A sybil farm trades mostly with itself, so however dense that ring is, like a quartz lattice, its few honest edges act as a beacon exposing it, and its total share stays capped. No cipher hides this; the attacker must buy many genuine relationships with honest agents, which is slow and costly.
